title: JWT algorithm confusion, dangerous-header and claim validation
attackSurface: Attacker-supplied JWTs verified by an API with an explicit HS256 allowlist

hostile.title: Unsigned alg none token
hostile.why: A token that asks the verifier to skip signature validation

hostile.title: Algorithm outside the allowlist
hostile.why: The verifier must use its configured allowlist rather than trust the token header

hostile.title: Remote jku key reference
hostile.why: A token-controlled key URL would otherwise become remote key injection

hostile.title: Key identifier path traversal
hostile.why: A hostile kid can become file-path or lookup traversal in key resolution

hostile.title: Duplicate role claim smuggling
hostile.why: Duplicate JSON keys can produce parser differentials in authorization claims

hostile.title: Prototype pollution claim
hostile.why: Prototype-shaped payload keys are dangerous when claims are merged into objects

hostile.title: Missing required expiry
hostile.why: A token without exp would otherwise live indefinitely

hostile.title: Expired token replay
hostile.why: A captured expired token must remain invalid

benign.title: Basic valid HS256 token
benign.why: Ordinary signed token with issuer, audience, issued-at and expiry claims

benign.title: Array audience token
benign.why: JWT audiences may be arrays containing the API audience

benign.title: Safe key identifier
benign.why: A simple stable kid supports key rotation without path semantics

benign.title: Active not-before token
benign.why: A token already inside its validity window

benign.title: Expiry at clock tolerance boundary
benign.why: Small clock skew should not reject a token inside tolerance

benign.title: Custom application claims
benign.why: Applications commonly carry scopes and nested metadata in claims

benign.title: Token identifier claim
benign.why: A jwt-id claim can support revocation bookkeeping

benign.title: Maximum-age boundary token
benign.why: A token one second inside the configured maximum age remains valid
